We need freshly generated electron-cyclotron (EC) profiles to inspect the
reference's heating and current conventions before coupling or training. The
[Primer](../primer.qmd) explains source coupling; terminology is in the
[Glossary](../glossary.qmd).

The owner approved one run with the corrected plotting library. The original
ITER numerical deck and GENRAY source remain unchanged. The run now reaches
the normal end of the solver and produces readable native output:
[the corrected EC reference completes in 83.16 s with readable native profiles]{.claim}[C-156](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-156){.cid .st-measured}.

We retained separate electron, ion and collisional heating channels and
each signed current definition. Heating volume integrals and the toroidal
current area integral agree with their matching stored totals to floating-point
precision. Other current definitions retain their upstream totals separately.
The single ray stops
when its remaining power reaches the deck's cutoff. Input hashes are unchanged,
stderr is empty, and raw outputs, snapshots and accounting records have bound
provenance.

The paired saved output uses an older GENRAY producer. Native coordinates and
bin volumes/areas match, allowing a direct descriptive comparison. The heating
and signed-current curves closely overlap at the displayed scale; the numerical
differences are retained without imposing a parity threshold.
Positive toroidal and negative parallel current remain distinct.

The saved file comes from upstream independently of our runner. Comparing it
uses the same reader for both files, so this is a descriptive regression check
and numerical accounting exercise. It is not independent physical validation.

![Fresh and older saved electron heating, toroidal current and parallel current
on native bins. Solid accent: corrected pilot; dashed grey: saved reference.
The curves overlap at this scale while their signed definitions remain
distinct.](../figures/m3_genray_profiles.svg){#fig-genray-pilot}

The PostScript device now opens and closes without errors. Its output renders
to a blank page, so this run does not establish plotted content or plotting
parity. A separate comparison figure is generated directly from the native
NetCDF profiles; it is not substituted for GENRAY's plotting output.

The bounded numerical pilot is complete. Production launch, heating/current
conversion, conservative radial mapping, fallback criteria and grouped sampling
still need to be settled before labelling or training. The ITER pedestal boundary
and matched transport comparison remain independent workstreams. Historical
suite reports are retained for unchanged tests. The repository checkpoint has
[56 focused checks pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-157](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-157){.cid .st-tested}; these fresh results are combined with retained reports when
generating the aggregate status.
That aggregate is not a fresh full-suite run. M3 remains in progress.
